description.value: The study examined changes in whole-brain functional connectivity associated with right inferior frontal cortex fMRI neurofeedback in adolescents with ADHD, including specificity relative to left parahippocampal gyrus neurofeedback and associations with clinical symptom changes.

spans.text: In the current study, we were particularly interested in the effects of rIFC self-regulation training in ADHD on functional connectivity with other brain networks.

design.value: A randomized controlled trial compared 18 ADHD adolescents receiving right inferior frontal cortex neurofeedback with 13 ADHD adolescents receiving control left parahippocampal gyrus neurofeedback. Functional connectivity was compared between the last and first neurofeedback runs using seed-based whole-brain correlation analyses.

spans.text: The original study was a randomized controlled trial testing the efficacy of fMRI-Neurofeedback of rIFC in 18 ADHD adolescents compared to a group of 13 ADHD adolescents who had to enhance another control region, the left parahippocampal gyrus.
Separate functional connectivity analyses were performed using these 2 clusters in Brodmann area 44 and Brodmann area 45 as seed regions.
